newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania president accused over jailed rival.
newsitem.headline: Albania president accused over jailed rival.

text.p: An Albanian former supreme court chief, in a newspaper commentary on Friday, accused President Sali Berisha of being behind the continued detention of opposition leader Fatos Nano, his strongest political rival.

The detention of Nano, who was jailed in 1994 on charges of embezzlement while prime minister, has been criticised by international human rights groups which say it casts a shadow over Albania's democracy.
Zef Brozi, who was sacked last year as supreme court chairman when he voiced doubts about Nano's trial, denied that he himself had been the force behind Nano's imprisonment.
"Fatos Nano...was sent to jail by (Sali) Berisha, the friend of (the last communist president Ramiz) Alia," Brozi wrote in Koha Jone newspaper.
"The prosecutors would not have arrested Nano if Berisha had not given the order," he said.
Brozi, who has been living in the United States since his dismissal, said Berisha had continued to put pressure on the judiciary to keep Nano behind bars.
Nano, 43, a socialist who was briefly prime minister in 1991, is currently held in the high-security Benca jail in a remote part of southern Albania and has three more years of his sentence to serve.
Brozi accused different judges by name of perverting the judicial system and said Berisha had exerted pressure on the judiciary last summer when Nano's case had come up for review.

"Why did the president mobilise the police, the government, the secret police, the Constitutional Court, prosecutor's office and judges, using them as his tools to sabotage Fatos Nano's judicial review...on July 26, 1995 and afterwards?", he wrote.

"Why doesn't Mr.Berisha release Fatos Nano? Perhaps he knows Nano is innocent and the president only pardons those who are guilty? On behalf of truth and humanity I ask Berisha to release innocent Nano," he said.
Nano was re-elected last month party leader of the Socialist party at a ground-breaking congress which scrapped Marxist doctrine.
The Socialists, who boycotted the country's third multi-party polls on May 26 and June 2 alleging government vote rigging, are Albania's second strongest political party.
But they refuse to take up the parliamentary seats they won, saying they do not accept the outcome of the election.
